title: A regular system of parameters is a regular sequence
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme] of dimension $d$ and let $x_1,\dots,x_d\in\mathfrak m$ generate $\mathfrak m$ (a regular system of parameters; in a regular local ring these are exactly the minimal sets of generators of $\mathfrak m$). Then $x_1,\dots,x_d$ is a regular sequence in $R$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence], and for each $0\le c\le d$ the ring $R/(x_1,\dots,x_c)$ is a regular local ring of dimension $d-c$. Since every permutation of $x_1,\dots,x_d$ again generates $\mathfrak m$, every permutation is a regular sequence.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00NQ (lemma-regular-ring-CM): 'Let R be a regular local ring and let x_1,...,x_d be a minimal set of generators for the maximal ideal m. Then x_1,...,x_d is a regular sequence, and each R/(x_1,...,x_c) is a regular local ring of dimension d-c'

proof.text: (The parenthetical: regular systems of parameters are the minimal sets of generators.) Let $\kappa=R/\mathfrak m$. $R$ is Noetherian and local [def-weil-regular-scheme]. (a) If $\mathfrak m$ is generated by $n$ elements then $d=\dim R\le n$ [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-local-dimension-le-generators]. Hence a set of $d$ generators of $\mathfrak m$ is minimal: a proper subset has fewer than $d$ elements and so cannot generate $\mathfrak m$. (b) Conversely let $y_1,\dots,y_n$ be a minimal set of generators of $\mathfrak m$ (no proper subset generates). Their images in $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2=\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m\mathfrak m$ are $\kappa$-linearly independent: if, say, $\bar y_n$ were a $\kappa$-combination of $\bar y_1,\dots,\bar y_{n-1}$, these would span $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m\mathfrak m$, so $y_1,\dots,y_{n-1}$ would generate the finitely generated $R$-module $\mathfrak m$ by Nakayama [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators], against minimality. They also span, so $n=\dim_\kappa\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$. Since $\mathfrak m$ is generated by some $d$ elements [def-weil-regular-scheme], whose images span $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$, $n\le d$; and $n\ge d$ by (a). So $n=d$: the minimal sets of generators of $\mathfrak m$ are exactly the sets of $d$ generators.

source.place: Algebra, Definition Tag 00KU (definition-regular-local) and Lemma Tag 00NO (lemma-regular-graded), proof: 'Let x_1..x_d be a minimal set of generators for the maximal ideal, see Definition'; written out with Proposition Tag 00KQ (proposition-dimension) and Nakayama, Lemma Tag 00DV (lemma-NAK)

proof.text: (Induction on $d$; the case $d=0$.) We prove the main claim (the $x_i$ form a regular sequence and $R/(x_1,\dots,x_c)$ is regular local of dimension $d-c$ for $0\le c\le d$) by induction on $d$, for all regular local rings of dimension $d$ simultaneously. The case $c=0$ is the hypothesis. If $d=0$, then $\mathfrak m$ is generated by the empty set, so $\mathfrak m=0$; the empty sequence is a regular sequence since condition (1) is vacuous and $R/(0)=R\neq0$ ($R$ is local) [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence], and the only quotient is $R$ itself.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00NQ (lemma-regular-ring-CM), induction implicit

proof.text: ($x_1$ is a nonzerodivisor.) Let $d\ge1$. $R$ is a domain [lem-sc-regular-local-domain]. Moreover $x_1\neq0$: otherwise $\mathfrak m$ would be generated by the $d-1$ elements $x_2,\dots,x_d$, so $\dim R\le d-1$ [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-local-dimension-le-generators], contradicting $\dim R=d$. A nonzero element of a domain is a nonzerodivisor, so multiplication by $x_1$ on $R$ is injective.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00NQ: 'Since R is a domain by Lemma 00NP (lemma-regular-domain) x_1 is a nonzerodivisor' (Stacks leaves x_1 != 0 implicit; it follows from minimality / Proposition Tag 00KQ)

proof.text: ($R'=R/x_1R$ is regular local of dimension $d-1$.) Since $x_1R\subseteq\mathfrak m$, $R'=R/x_1R$ is a local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m'=\mathfrak m/x_1R$ [lem-weil-pbc-quotient-local-structure], Noetherian as a quotient of the Noetherian ring $R$ [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-image-noetherian]. The images $\bar x_1=0,\bar x_2,\dots,\bar x_d$ generate $\mathfrak m'$, so $\bar x_2,\dots,\bar x_d$ generate $\mathfrak m'$. As $x_1\in\mathfrak m$ is a nonzerodivisor (step 3), $\dim R'+1=\dim R=d$ [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-quotient-nonzerodivisor], so $\dim R'=d-1$ and $\mathfrak m'$ is generated by $\dim R'$ elements: $R'$ is a regular local ring of dimension $d-1$ [def-weil-regular-scheme] with $\bar x_2,\dots,\bar x_d$ generating its maximal ideal. (Stacks uses only the inequality $\dim R'\ge d-1$ of Lemma 00KW together with $\mathfrak m'$ being generated by $d-1$ elements; the equality for a nonzerodivisor gives the same.)

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00NQ: 'R/x_1R is a Noetherian local ring of dimension >= d-1 by Lemma 00KW (lemma-one-equation) with x_2..x_d generating the maximal ideal. Hence it is a regular local ring by definition'

proof.text: (Induction step.) By the induction hypothesis applied to $R'$ and $\bar x_2,\dots,\bar x_d$ (step 4): $\bar x_2,\dots,\bar x_d$ is a regular sequence in $R'$ and $R'/(\bar x_2,\dots,\bar x_c)$ is regular local of dimension $(d-1)-(c-1)=d-c$ for $1\le c\le d$. For $1\le i\le d+1$ the third isomorphism theorem gives $R/(x_1,\dots,x_{i-1})\cong R'/(\bar x_2,\dots,\bar x_{i-1})$ as $R$-modules (and as rings), with $x_i$ acting as $\bar x_i$. Hence $R/(x_1,\dots,x_c)$ is regular local of dimension $d-c$ for $c\ge1$; and in the definition of a regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]: $x_1$ is a nonzerodivisor on $R$ (step 3), for $i\ge2$ multiplication by $x_i$ on $R/(x_1,\dots,x_{i-1})$ is multiplication by $\bar x_i$ on $R'/(\bar x_2,\dots,\bar x_{i-1})$, which is injective, and $R/(x_1,\dots,x_d)\cong R'/(\bar x_2,\dots,\bar x_d)\neq0$. So $x_1,\dots,x_d$ is a regular sequence in $R$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00NQ (the induction left implicit in Stacks)

proof.text: (Permutations.) For a permutation $\sigma$ of $\{1,\dots,d\}$, the elements $x_{\sigma(1)},\dots,x_{\sigma(d)}$ are again $d=\dim R$ elements of $\mathfrak m$ generating $\mathfrak m$, so steps 2-5 applied to them show that they form a regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence].
